{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI / Company Internet Site Agreement)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (for the Company / Customer)

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of Exhibit 10.2. The agreement is a hosting and development arrangement under which HDI builds, operates and hosts the Site, holds our Content, Marks, user information and customer data, and takes a 30% revenue share. The commercial fee structure is favourable to us (pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit), but the risk-allocation architecture of the agreement is largely absent.

Five of the playbook's core protections have no clause at all: **intellectual property ownership**, **limitation of liability**, **vendor indemnification**, **vendor insurance**, and **post-termination transition assistance and data return**. In a arrangement where HDI develops the Site and holds our Content and customer data, the silence on ownership and indemnity is the single most serious exposure — HDI could assert developer/host claims over Site deliverables and Site data, and we have no IP infringement defence for a Site we did not build.

Separately, several clauses that do exist run against us beyond our fallback tolerances: the Section 4.2 Termination Payment (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) is an uncapped exit fee that routinely exceeds a year's fees; the Section 6.1 exclusivity and non-compete covenants are elastic in scope and open-ended in duration because the term auto-renews indefinitely; Section 10.3 permits HDI to assign freely, including to a competitor; Section 9 contains no performance warranty of any kind; and the Section 1.4 access grant omits our affiliates and contractors and is silent on revocability.

Governing law (New York, Section 10.5), the absence of MFN obligations, the absence of minimum purchase commitments, and the absence of a non-solicit are all compliant and require no redline.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | No provision (reviewed alongside § 1.4) | No ownership or IP clause anywhere; Content, Marks, Site deliverables and Site/customer data unallocated. Inserting Proprietary Rights section (Company ownership; assignment of Site Deliverables with HDI licence-back). |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | No provision (Sections 9 and 10 silent) | Unlimited direct and consequential liability for both Parties. Inserting mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped carve-outs. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10.3 | Bare successors-and-assigns clause with no consent standard; HDI may assign to a competitor. Adding consent gate, competitor bar, and Company freedom to assign to affiliates/M&A successors. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | Access/use grant omits affiliates and contractors with no mechanism to add them, and is silent on revocability. Extending to affiliates/contractors, making irrevocable during term absent our uncured material breach, and confirming transfer to a successor. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (with § 6.2 carve-out) | Elastic scope ("substantially similar" products, "similar" companies), no 12-month outside limit given indefinite auto-renewal, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Narrowing to Deerskin Products with a 12-month cap and carve-outs. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 4.1 | 90-day non-renewal window exceeds our 60-day fallback ceiling. Cutting the Company's window to 30 days (HDI's 90 days retained) and adding a 60-day renewal reminder. Renewal is on same terms, so no uplift cap needed. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | No provision (§ 4 and § 10.7 silent) | No return, export or deletion of Company data and no wind-down assistance, in an arrangement where HDI holds our Content and customer data. Inserting Section 4.3 (up to 6 months' assistance, data return within 30 days, deletion with certification). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 9(a)–(b) | Section 9 contains only a mutual authority representation and a Globix acknowledgment; no performance standard, no conformance to documentation, no malicious-code warranty, no remedy. Adding 90-day services warranty, 12-month conformance warranty, legal compliance, no malicious code, and repair/replace/refund. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 10.5 | New York law, our preferred position, with conflicts principles disclaimed; no arbitration or foreign forum. The absence of an express exclusive New York County venue sentence is noted only. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | No provision (§§ 3.1–3.4 reviewed) | No MFN construct anywhere; fees are a fixed 30% revenue share. The § 6.1 exclusivity is addressed under the exclusivity rule, not duplicated here. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 3.1 (with §§ 4.1–4.2 reviewed) | Fees payable solely on actual Net Sales above $11,000/month; no floor, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic, and a rolling one-year term. The § 4.2 exit fee is assessed under the LD and T4C rules. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | No provision (§§ 5.4, 6, 10 reviewed) | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds the Company; employment references are incidental only. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 | Notice, business-hours timing and cost allocation are favourable, but there is no frequency limit, the inspection is by HDI's own General Manager rather than an independent auditor, and no bar on system access. Adding annual cap, independent confidentiality-bound auditor and no-system-access limit. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (with §§ 4.1–4.2) | Exclusivity runs for an indefinitely renewing term with no performance-based release and an exit fee gating departure. Taking the fallback: 12 months from the Effective Date, confined to Deerskin Products, lapsing automatically on any HDI service level or delivery date failure. Sits at the fallback once amended. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | No provision (§ 9 runs straight into § 10) | No HDI indemnity for third-party IP infringement in the Site it builds and hosts, breach of law, data/Content security incidents, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct — walk-away territory under the rule. Inserting Section 9A with standard claim procedure and a narrow reciprocal Company indemnity. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | No provision (§ 10 reviewed) | No insurance obligation on either party despite HDI operating the Site and handling customer order data and e-mail lists. Inserting Section 10.9 (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp, certificates on request); fallback limits offered in comment. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 4.2 | Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 on any Company termination routinely exceeds a year's 30% revenue-share fees, failing the 3-month fallback cap. Adding a lesser-of cap at 3 months' § 3.1 fees and sole-liquidated-amount language. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | §§ 4.1, 4.2(a) | We have no mid-term convenience right, and any Company termination triggers the uncapped exit fee payable in eight quarterly instalments. Adding an express Company convenience right on 90 days' notice and capping the Termination Payment at 3 months' § 3.1 payments. |

## Walk-away items

Two findings reach walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **No vendor indemnity (INDEMN, § 9 / § 10 gap).** The complete absence of an HDI IP infringement indemnity is expressly identified as walk-away under the rule. HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site; we cannot carry unallocated third-party infringement, breach-of-law or data security exposure for a platform we did not build.
2. **No limitation of liability at all (LOL-CAP).** Uncapped direct and consequential liability on both sides, combined with the absence of any indemnity or insurance, leaves the Company's exposure unbounded. A mutual cap with the standard uncapped carve-outs is a condition of signature.

**Near walk-away — treat as escalation-worthy:** the absence of any HDI insurance (INSURANCE) falls below even our fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) for a vendor processing customer data, and the absence of any IP ownership allocation (IP) leaves our Content, Marks and Site data claimable by HDI as developer and host.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the five insertions (IP/Proprietary Rights, limitation of liability at new § 10.9, indemnity at new § 9A, insurance, and transition assistance/data return at new § 4.3) and the amendments to §§ 1.4, 3.4, 4.1, 4.2, 6.1, 9 and 10.3, each with a `[Playbook]` comment stating our position and, where noted above, the fallback.
2. **Sequence the negotiation** around the two walk-away items first (indemnity and liability cap), then the IP ownership allocation and insurance, then the exit-fee and exclusivity economics.
3. **Confirm commercial input** on the § 4.2 Termination Payment: we should validate trailing Net Sales against the $800,000 threshold so we can quantify the current exit exposure when we propose the 3-month cap.
4. **Confirm exclusivity tolerance** with the business on § 6.1 — we are proposing the fallback (12 months, Deerskin Products only, automatic lapse on HDI service level or delivery date failure) rather than deletion, on the basis that HDI carries the development and hosting burden and gives a reciprocal covenant that benefits us.
5. **Hold as no-change:** governing law (§ 10.5), the absence of MFN, minimum commitments and any non-solicit. We would accept an exclusive New York County venue sentence only if the drafting is reopened for other reasons."}
